decisions.executionNote: Coin is in the left workspace, bank on right. Begin left elbow-up approach and downward gripper rotation; adapt from RGB rather than reference coordinates.
Continue left approach above the holder, with small continuous wrist rotation toward a vertical coin pinch.
Advance toward the coin while maintaining elbow-up continuity and clearance above the holder.
Bring left gripper above the coin and match its visible slanted plane with a downward approach.
Complete downward alignment above left coin; keep fingers open and inspect before descending to pinch.
Use wrist view to center coin between fingers: small lateral correction and 1 cm descent, partly closing to inspect pinch alignment.
Coin edge is centered at the pinch line in the left wrist image. Close fully without further approach, then test retention by lifting.
Lift coin vertically from holder with left gripper kept closed; inspect whether coin follows.
Coin appears displaced from the pinch rather than retained. Pause above the holder and reopen to assess its resting position before a corrected grasp.
The coin slipped and is moving across the table. Track from above with open left fingers while it settles.
Coin is now flat and stationary. Lower the open left gripper above its estimated center; account for wrist-camera parallax before attempting an edge pinch.
Approach the flat coin slowly, centering it laterally and narrowing the jaws while remaining above the surface.
At the surface, stop descent and close slowly around the flat coin's rim. Retention remains uncertain until a lift test.
The closing tips nudged rather than captured the flat coin. Reopen and advance the pinch line over its center, slightly clearing the table.
Advance a little farther over the flat coin and lower 5 mm, then close gradually around opposite rim edges rather than its near edge.
Coin lies between the jaws behind their tips. Finish closing and begin a very small lift to test rim retention.
Lift with left jaws fully closed and inspect whether the coin follows the gripper or remains on the tabletop.
Coin remained on the table. Recenter using the calibrated head view and level the downward jaws for another slow rim grasp.
Fine-center the flat disk at the jaw tips and descend only 6 mm before final closure, avoiding a long sweeping motion.
Disk is centered at the pinch line. Close at the rim with only 2 mm additional descent, then test with a 3 mm lift.
Coin appears caught between both finger tips. Lift vertically with closure maintained and verify retention visually.
Coin is visibly retained. Lift clear and rotate it upright while bringing it toward a center handoff, keeping left link6 within the left workspace.
Continue left coin reorientation toward an upright handoff. Begin raising and turning the right open gripper for an overhead face pinch.
Keep the retained coin secure while bringing it upright toward center. Raise right open gripper toward an above-coin handoff pose without crossing the arms.
Finish presenting the upright coin near center with the left arm; bring right open fingers above the coin for a face-to-face pinch.
Previous chunk was rejected without motion. Halve left increments to preserve joint continuity near the handoff orientation.
Replan from the two executed steps. Use smaller left wrist increments while right approaches above the center handoff with fingers open.
Continue upright coin presentation and move the right open gripper above the exposed upper rim, keeping each arm on its own side.
Finish leveling the left-held upright coin and continue the right overhead approach. Keep a small center separation between arm links.
Right continuity guard stopped the approach. Lower the held coin to a more reachable handoff height and reduce right increments; no compensation for discarded steps.
Coin remains in the left rim grasp. Fine-align right fingers above its upper edge, with small motions and both link6 positions staying on their own sides.
Right approach reached an IK limit and may have disturbed the coin. Lower the handoff to regain reachability and separate the upper fingers from the coin before realignment.
No motion executed in rejected chunk. Reduce right lowering to 3 mm steps and lower the left-held coin away from the upper jaw.
Coin remains held but has tilted flat. Center the right overhead jaws around its opposite rim, descending slowly with left grip maintained.
Fine-center the right pinch from its wrist image and close around the exposed coin rim while the left arm remains stationary.
Right jaws appear engaged at the coin. Open the left gripper gradually, maintaining right closure, then separate slightly to verify the handoff visually.
Coin is now visibly retained upright by the right gripper. Separate the arms, withdraw left, and carry the coin toward the right bank while rotating its plane toward the slot.
Carry the upright coin laterally toward the bank with clearance. Continue rotating the coin plane to match the slot and retract the empty left arm.
Continue high-clearance transport and yaw alignment to the visible slot. Retract left toward its starting pose with continuous elbow-up motion.
Reduce right translation and yaw after the continuity interruption. Keep the coin high while approaching the bank; continue left retraction.
Approach above the bank slot using calibrated head position and wrist alignment; preserve coin closure and finish returning the empty left arm.
Bring the held coin directly above the slot and finish matching its long-axis direction. Keep height for a final wrist-camera alignment check.
Slot and coin are nearly aligned in the right wrist view. Make a small yaw correction and slow 25 mm descent, keeping the coin closed; settle left at origin.
Refine alignment from wrist image: move back along the slot and slightly toward its centerline while descending another 15 mm. Keep coin retained.
The coin visibly tilted on contact rather than entering cleanly. Lift 3 cm with grip closed to clear the bank and assess retention before realigning.
Coin has slipped away from the right gripper. Reopen and let it settle before attempting recovery; do not continue insertion blindly.
Coin is stationary on the bank shoulder. Move the open right gripper above it for a careful recovery grasp, avoiding the slot rim.
Lower vertically above the loose coin while keeping jaws fully open. Use the change in wrist view to distinguish height parallax from lateral error.
Vertical approach moved the coin toward the pinch line as expected. Continue slowly and narrow the jaws above the rim, with a small lateral centering correction.
Coin is centered laterally but still ahead of the fingertips. Lower in 3.5 mm increments and narrow gently to reach its rim without sweeping it.
Tracking residual indicates contact with the bank. Stop downward pressure, raise slightly and shift toward the coin rim before closing.
The rim is at the fingertip line but offset sideways. Recenter gently, lower only 3 mm, and close for a recovery lift test.
The tips appear above the coin rather than gripping its rim. Reopen and approach 11 mm lower in small increments, watching for bank contact.
The rim is now between both fingers. Finish closure without further descent and test retention with a small vertical lift.
Coin is offset behind and beside the closed tips, not securely retained. Reopen and reposition the pinch line over its center before trying again.
Coin slipped off the bank onto the table. Clear the bank and track its resting position with the open right gripper before another recovery.
Coin has settled flat on the table. Move above its calibrated head-view center and lower with open jaws, stopping well above the surface for final alignment.
Use wrist feedback to correct the coin's lateral offset while descending toward a table-level rim pinch. Keep the approach slow and jaws mostly open.
Center the table coin from wrist feedback and level the downward fingers. Approach the rim at table height before final closure.
The disk is at the correct depth but slightly right of the pinch center. Correct laterally, close at the rim, and keep the arm stationary for retention inspection.
Test the new rim pinch with a slow vertical lift, maintaining full closure and watching whether the coin follows both fingertips.
Coin stayed on the table and shifted sideways. Reopen, correct the visible offset, and approach level before closing again.
Disk is nearly centered. Make a millimeter-scale correction and lower 5 mm, then close around opposite rim edges without lifting yet.
Test this centered rim grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping closure commanded and checking coin motion against the background.
